newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul Bancorp sees $13.65 mln Q3 charge.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul Bancorp sees $13.65 mln Q3 charge.

text.p: St. Paul Bancorp Inc said Tuesday it expects to take a one-time pre-tax charge of $13.65 million related to its mandated contribution to replenish the FDIC's Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF).

"Based upon the information that the FDIC and the Congressional document says, it is our best estimate of it," chief financial officer Robert Parke said of the expected charge. He spoke in a telephone interview.
The $4.34 billion asset thrift reported earnings of $9.1 million, or $0.46 a share, in the 1995 third quarter.
Parke would not say how the charge would convert into share earnings.
On Tuesday, the FDIC approved a one-time $4.5 billion assessment on the U.S. thrift industry to recapitalize the fund, which insures depositors at savings and loan institutions.

The one-time special assessment equals 65.7 cents on every $100 in insured deposits that thrifts hold. The FDIC also proposed to cut the premiums savings and loans pay twice yearly to fund SAIF once it reaches government mandated levels.
